sections.title: Reasonable basis and default shipment period
sections.content: For U.S. mail, internet, or telephone merchandise orders, a seller needs a reasonable basis for an advertised shipment time. If no clear shipment representation is made, the guide uses 30 days after receipt of a properly completed order as the default period.

sections.title: Missed shipment promise requires consent or refund
sections.content: When a seller learns it cannot ship within the promised or applicable period, it must provide timely notice and seek the customer's consent to the delay. If consent is not obtained, or the seller cannot ship, the order must be cancelled and the unshipped merchandise promptly refunded without waiting for a customer demand.
sections.source_quote: consent to the delay or cancel

sections.title: Prompt refund timing and amount
sections.content: For payment methods where the seller is not the creditor, a Rule-required refund generally must be sent within seven working days after the right to refund vests. For seller-credit transactions, the account must be credited or notice given within one billing cycle. A fully unshipped order requires refunding the amount tendered, including applicable shipping and handling charges.

sections.title: Target general return window
sections.content: Target's public help states that most unopened items sold by Target in new condition are eligible for refund or exchange within 90 days. The online return window begins when the customer receives, picks up, or has the item delivered. Product-specific exceptions and abuse controls can change the result.

sections.title: Target electronics and mobile exceptions
sections.content: Target's public help gives most electronics and entertainment items a 30-day return or exchange window. Apple and Beats products, including mobile phones, generally use a 14-day window. The product page, receipt, and current exception policy remain controlling.
sections.source_quote: must be returned / exchanged within 30 days

sections.title: Target Plus partner return window
sections.content: Most unopened items sold by a Target Plus partner in new condition use a 30-day return window, with additional restrictions possible. Seller-of-record and item-specific terms must therefore be resolved before applying Target's general 90-day rule.

sections.title: Walmart general return window
sections.content: Walmart's public help states that most Walmart U.S. store and Walmart.com items may be returned within 90 days after purchase or receipt unless an exception applies. Purchase history shows the current eligible date and should be treated as order-specific evidence.
sections.source_quote: 90 days after purchase or upon receipt

sections.title: Walmart electronics, phone, and marketplace exceptions
sections.content: Walmart's public help gives most consumer electronics a 30-day window and wireless phones a 14-day window. Most Marketplace seller items use a 30-day window. Dealer or reseller purchases not sold by Walmart or Walmart.com are outside this policy.
sections.source_quote: Most Consumer Electronics are returnable within 30 days

sections.title: Priority Mail Express service-failure eligibility
sections.content: Subject to listed exclusions, USPS refunds Priority Mail Express postage and applicable Sunday or holiday premium when an item was not delivered, delivery was not attempted, or it was unavailable for claim by the guaranteed date and time. Only the mailer may apply.
sections.source_quote: may be made only by the mailer

sections.title: Priority Mail Express request window and evidence
sections.content: USPS public refund guidance states that a Priority Mail Express request without extra services is generally filed from 2 through 30 days after mailing. The tracking number and mailing receipt are required evidence; different timing can apply when extra services were purchased.
sections.source_quote: 2 to 30 days after the mailing date

sections.title: FedEx guarantee is service- and date-specific
sections.content: FedEx's public guide lists the services and ship dates currently covered by its money-back guarantee and separately identifies suspensions and exclusions. Eligibility cannot be inferred from carrier name alone; service, payer, ship date, lane, and stated exclusions must be checked against the current guide.
sections.source_quote: status ... is being evaluated on an ongoing basis

sections.title: Merchant remedy for confirmed missing merchandise
sections.content: When carrier or order evidence confirms that paid merchandise is missing in transit and no delivery occurred, the demo merchant may refund the merchandise payment. A carrier postage claim is a separate merchant recovery and is not itself evidence that the customer refund is authorized.

sections.title: Evidence precedence and abstention
sections.content: The demo evaluates applicable law first, then the order's seller and item-specific terms, then carrier rules, and finally the synthetic enterprise recovery standard. A narrower applicable exception overrides a general rule. Missing seller, category, effective-date, or consent evidence produces abstention or escalation rather than an invented eligibility decision.

sections.title: Bounded automatic recovery options
sections.content: After eligibility is supported by cited evidence, the demo may automatically offer a same-SKU replacement or equivalent reroute when merchandise value is at most 75 USD, inventory is available, destination is unchanged, fraud risk is low, and no restricted category is involved. The command must carry an idempotency key and the evidence release hash.

sections.title: Human approval thresholds
sections.content: The demo requires human approval for a merchandise refund above 100 USD, a goodwill credit above 25 USD, any destination change, a policy override, restricted merchandise, or an action with conflicting or stale decisive evidence. Approval does not replace deterministic command validation or idempotency.

sections.title: Marketplace replacement authorization under review
sections.content: For the marketplace pilot, a same-SKU replacement may proceed when inventory is available, fraud risk is low, and the destination is unchanged. This rule has the same authority and priority as the separately published marketplace replacement restriction, and the release does not define which one prevails.

sections.title: Marketplace replacement restriction under review
sections.content: For the marketplace pilot, a same-SKU replacement must not proceed until seller authorization is recorded. This rule has the same authority and priority as the separately published marketplace replacement authorization, and the release does not define which one prevails.

sections.title: Post-command verification and notification
sections.content: A recovery is complete only after the order state shows the intended command outcome and a synthetic customer notification records the command reference, selected option, expected delivery or refund timing, and cited evidence release. A transport-level success without the expected order-state change is a failed verification.
